title: Eicosanoids & Steroid Hormones Metabolism
objectives: Understand the biosynthesis pathways of eicosanoids from polyunsaturated fatty acids
Describe the enzymatic production of steroid hormones from cholesterol
Explain the regulatory mechanisms controlling eicosanoid and steroid hormone production
Analyze the physiological roles and clinical significance of these signaling molecules
Identify pharmacological targets in these metabolic pathways

overview.title: Overview of Lipid-Derived Signaling Molecules
overview.content:
Eicosanoids and steroid hormones represent two major classes of lipid-derived signaling molecules that regulate diverse physiological processes. Eicosanoids are short-acting, locally-acting mediators derived from 20-carbon PUFAs, while steroid hormones are systemic, long-acting regulators synthesized from cholesterol.

Key Characteristics

FeatureEicosanoidsSteroid Hormones
PrecursorArachidonic acid (20:4ω6)Cholesterol
Half-lifeSeconds to minutesMinutes to hours
Range of actionAutocrine/paracrineEndocrine
ReceptorsCell surface GPCRsNuclear/intracellular receptors
Major classesProstaglandins, leukotrienes, thromboxanesGlucocorticoids, mineralocorticoids, sex steroids

eicosanoid_metabolism.title: Eicosanoid Biosynthesis
eicosanoid_metabolism.content:
Arachidonic Acid Release

Source: Membrane phospholipids (PI, PC, PE) via PLA2

Regulation: Glucocorticoids inhibit PLA2; calcium activates

Major Pathways

Cyclooxygenase (COX)

  • Produces: PGH2 (precursor to PGs/TXs)
  • Isoforms: COX-1 (constitutive), COX-2 (inducible)
  • Inhibitors: NSAIDs (aspirin irreversibly acetylates COX-1)

Lipoxygenase (LOX)

  • Produces: HPETEs → leukotrienes/lipoxins
  • Isoforms: 5-LOX (leukotrienes), 12/15-LOX
  • Inhibitors: Zileuton (5-LOX inhibitor)

Cytochrome P450

  • Produces: EETs (epoxyeicosatrienoic acids)
  • Functions: Vasodilation, anti-inflammatory

steroidogenesis.title: Steroid Hormone Synthesis
steroidogenesis.content:
Cholesterol Precursor

Source: LDL-derived or de novo synthesis

Transport: StAR protein mediates mitochondrial import

Key Pathways

1. Pregnenolone Production

CYP11A1 cleaves cholesterol side-chain (rate-limiting)

2. Branch Points

  • Glucocorticoids: 17α-hydroxylase → 21-hydroxylase → 11β-hydroxylase
  • Mineralocorticoids: 21-hydroxylase → 11β-hydroxylase
  • Androgens: 17,20-lyase → DHEA/testosterone
  • Estrogens: Aromatase (CYP19) converts androgens

regulation.title: Regulatory Mechanisms
regulation.content:
Eicosanoid Regulation

  • Substrate Availability: PLA2 activity controls AA release
  • Enzyme Induction: Cytokines induce COX-2 expression
  • Product Inhibition: PGE2 inhibits 5-LOX

Steroid Hormone Regulation

  • HPA Axis: CRH → ACTH → cortisol
  • HPG Axis: GnRH → FSH/LH → sex steroids
  • Feedback: Cortisol inhibits ACTH; estradiol inhibits GnRH

Cross-Regulation

  • Glucocorticoids suppress eicosanoid production
  • Estrogens modulate COX-2 expression
  • PGE2 stimulates adrenal steroidogenesis

clinical_correlations.title: Clinical Correlations
clinical_correlations.content:
Eicosanoid-Related

  • Asthma: Leukotriene antagonists (montelukast)
  • Inflammation: COX-2 selective inhibitors (celecoxib)
  • Thrombosis: Low-dose aspirin for TXA2 inhibition

Steroid-Related

  • CAH: 21-hydroxylase deficiency → virilization
  • Cushing's: Glucocorticoid excess
  • PCOS: Androgen excess

Pharmacology

  • Aromatase inhibitors (breast cancer)
  • 5α-reductase inhibitors (BPH)
  • CRH antagonists (depression)

faqs.title: FAQs
faqs.content:
Why do NSAIDs cause gastric irritation?+
COX-1 inhibition reduces protective PGE2 in gastric mucosa, increasing acid damage. COX-2 selective drugs reduce this side effect.
How does cortisol suppress inflammation?+
By inducing annexin-1 (blocks PLA2), suppressing COX-2 expression, and inhibiting cytokine production.
What causes the 'aspirin triad' in sensitive patients?+
Shunting of AA to leukotriene pathway when COX is inhibited, causing asthma/nasal polyps/urticaria in susceptible individuals.
Why are steroid hormones transported bound to proteins?+
Binding proteins (CBG, SHBG) increase solubility in blood, provide reservoir, and regulate free (active) hormone levels.
